units.title: From the jiko: four Kenyan classics

lessons.title: Sukuma wiki
learn: Slicing greens thin so they cook fast
Keeping greens bright instead of overcooked
ingredients: 1 bunch of sukuma (collard greens), about 300 g

steps.text: Wash the leaves, cut out the thick stems, then roll the leaves up and slice them thinly
steps.tip: Thin ribbons cook in minutes and stay tender.

steps.text: Fry the onion in the oil over a medium heat

timer.doneness: until soft and just turning golden

steps.text: Add the tomatoes and a pinch of salt

timer.doneness: until they have broken down into a thick sauce

steps.text: Add the greens and toss them through the sauce, uncovered

timer.doneness: until the leaves are dark green and tender with a little bite

steps.tip: Stop before they turn olive brown. Overcooked sukuma loses its taste.

steps.text: Taste for salt and serve with ugali or chapati

lessons.title: Ugali
learn: Knowing when ugali is firm enough to turn out

steps.text: Bring the water to the boil in a heavy pan
Turn the heat to medium and whisk in about a third of the flour

timer.doneness: until it thickens like porridge and starts to bubble

steps.tip: Add it slowly while stirring and you won't get lumps.

steps.text: Add the rest of the flour bit by bit, pressing and folding it with a wooden spoon

timer.doneness: until it's stiff and smooth and pulls away from the sides

steps.text: Shape it into a mound, turn the heat to low and leave it
steps.detail: Turn it over once halfway so both sides firm up.

timer.doneness: until it smells toasty and a thin skin forms underneath

steps.text: Turn it out onto a plate and serve hot

lessons.title: Chapati
learn: Kneading and resting a soft dough
Coiling the dough so the chapati comes out in layers
ingredients: 375 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting

steps.text: Mix the flour, salt and sugar, then add the warm water and 2 tbsp oil and bring it together into a soft dough
Knead the dough on a floured worktop

timer.doneness: until it's smooth and springs back when you press it

steps.text: Cover the dough with a bowl and leave it to rest

timer.doneness: until it feels soft and stretches without tearing

steps.tip: Resting relaxes the dough, so it rolls out thin without shrinking back.

steps.text: Cut it into 8 pieces. Roll each one thin, brush with oil, roll it up like a rope and coil it into a snail
steps.detail: The oil between the coils is what gives you soft layers.

steps.text: Roll each coil out into a circle about 20 cm across
Cook a chapati in a dry pan over a medium-high heat

timer.doneness: until bubbles rise and the underside has brown spots

steps.text: Flip it, brush the top with a little oil and cook the other side

timer.doneness: until both sides are golden with darker spots

steps.tip: Stack the cooked chapatis under a clean towel so they stay soft while you cook the rest.

lessons.title: Beef pilau
learn: Browning onions deep for pilau's colour
Cooking rice in a spiced broth until it's fluffy
ingredients: 500 g stewing beef, cut into 3 cm pieces
4 garlic cloves and a thumb of ginger, crushed
2 tbsp pilau masala and 1 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp salt and about 1 litre of water

steps.text: Simmer the beef with the salt in 1 litre of water in a covered pan

timer.doneness: until a piece breaks apart easily with a fork

steps.tip: Keep the broth. It's the cooking liquid for the rice.

steps.text: Lift out the beef and measure 750 ml of the broth, topping it up with water if needed
Fry the onions in the oil in a heavy pan over a medium heat

timer.doneness: until they're a deep golden brown

steps.tip: Don't rush this. The browner the onions, the darker and tastier the pilau.

steps.text: Stir in the cumin seeds, garlic, ginger and pilau masala
Add the tomatoes

timer.doneness: until they've softened into the spices

steps.text: Add the beef, the rice and the 750 ml of broth, stir once and bring to the boil
Cover tightly, turn the heat right down and cook

timer.doneness: until the broth has been absorbed and the rice is tender

steps.text: Take it off the heat and leave it covered

timer.doneness: until the grains are dry and separate

steps.tip: Fluff it with a fork before serving, and serve with kachumbari if you have it.
